# Iteration 32: D2L reduction depth and resource tradeoffs

gfx936 physical GPU7, INT8 NT -> INT32, no scale. Compare dense K32/64/128 ping-pong with native 64-bit LDS fragments; also smaller 128x256 and 128x128 output blocks. Retained experimental; no production change.

32 full-range INT8/FP64 checks and 40 performance-output checks pass. Full-range tests include tails, strides, unequal group lengths, full input copies and guards; performance uses 3 samples warmup2/repeat5, median.

Compiled metadata: K32 256x256 eight-wave candidates use170 VGPRs/thread (shift0:172), no private segment; K64 256x256 b64-read candidate uses184 VGPRs/thread; K128 128x128 uses140. This is compiler resource metadata, not measured occupancy. The earlier v30 four-wave 256x256 uses256 VGPRs/thread and440 private bytes/thread; resource pressure is evidenced rather than inferred solely from timing.

K32 reduces LDS allocation and VGPR count but regresses throughput to about268-286 TOPS on these samples. Smaller output blocks also regress. Reducing resource use alone does not solve the runtime gap; the load/compute schedule still needs work. Raw self-generated ISA and notes remain in build/own_isa_v30 and build/own_isa_v32.
